get.description:
Recent inquiries for this tenant, newest first.

Exists because a graph runner needs something to run on, and the alternative -- typing an
id copied from a log -- is not a demo. `limit` is clamped rather than trusted: an
unbounded list is the cheapest way to make a picker load a whole table.

post.description: Resume a pipeline that stopped at the human gate. Requires a reviewer role.
Resume a halted run. The node is derived from persisted state, not from the request.

get.description:
What the tenant's corpus actually contains.

The knowledge page needs this to distinguish "the corpus is empty, seed it" from "the
corpus does not cover your question". Both produce a refusal, and they call for opposite
actions -- without this endpoint the page would have to guess.

post.description: Load the bundled SOP corpus. Idempotent: re-seeding creates no duplicates.

get.description: Latency, token and cost accounting. Arithmetic over recorded rows, no model involved.

AgentAskIn.title: AgentAskIn
AgentAskIn.description:
Ask the tool-calling agent a question.

`inquiry_id` is optional and only a hint: the policy also reads it from the question
text, and every tool re-checks it against the caller's tenant.

GraphResumeIn.title: GraphResumeIn
GraphResumeIn.description:
Re-enter a halted graph run at the node it stopped at.

No `start_node` here on purpose: the resume point is derived from persisted state, so a
client cannot ask to skip a gate by naming the node after it.

GraphRunIn.title: GraphRunIn
GraphRunIn.description: Start the LangGraph pipeline on an existing inquiry.

OrchestrateContinueIn.title: OrchestrateContinueIn
OrchestrateContinueIn.description: Continue after a human decision at a gate.

OrchestrateIn.title: OrchestrateIn
OrchestrateIn.description:
Start-or-resume input for the unified pipeline.

`inquiry_id` is required: the pipeline operates on an inquiry that already exists, so
there is exactly one way an inquiry enters the system (the inbound-message endpoint)
rather than two competing ones.

ProspectImportIn.title: ProspectImportIn
ProspectImportIn.description:
A purchased or exported list, not a search result.

`source` and `data_origin` are required and non-trivial: a list whose provenance nobody
can name is exactly the list that cannot be lawfully emailed, so it is refused at the
door rather than stored and sorted out later.
